title: JWT vs session token trace event state
description: Shape of the `state` field for jwt-vs-session-token trace events.

scheme.description: Where the truth lives: signed claims carried by the client, or a record behind an opaque id.

clock.description: Model time in minutes since the run started.

accessTtl.description: How long an issued credential stays valid, in minutes.

checkAudience.description: Whether services refuse a token whose `aud` names somebody else.

denyListEnabled.description: Whether the issuer keeps a revocation list — the state a stateless token needs to be revocable.

trustAlgHeader.description: The bug: the verifier uses the algorithm named by the token it is verifying.

services.description: The services that verify credentials, and how often each has done so.

credential.description: The credential currently under the microscope; null before anything is issued.

kind.description: A compact JWT, or a meaningless session id.

raw.description: The exact bytes the client puts on the wire.

size.description: Length of `raw` — what every request has to carry.

revealed.description: True for a JWT, whose segments are always readable; false for an opaque id.

tampered.description: Whether the client edited the payload or the header after it was signed.

signature.description: The third segment; empty when the header claims `alg: none`.

sessionStore.description: Records the server remembers. Always empty in JWT mode — that is the point.

denied.description: Revoked token ids the issuer still has to remember.

truth.description: What the database says about each user right now — the only current truth.

active.description: False once the account has been switched off.

action.description: What the current step is doing.

kind.description: Which part of the credential's life is running.

actor.description: Who is acting: the issuer, a service, an admin or whoever holds the value.

detail.description: The user, token id or claim edit this step is about.

checks.description: The five checks every verification walks, in order, with the verdict of each.

id.description: parse = well-formed; source = decoded locally or looked up; trust = signature or our own record; claims = exp and aud; revoked = still supposed to work.

status.description: pending = never reached; breach = it let through what it should have stopped.

detail.description: Bare token behind the verdict: a claim value, a signature or a reason.

status.description: HTTP status the service answered with; null when the step is not a request.

decision.description: breach = the request was served and should not have been.

reason.description: Technical code for the refusal or the breach; null when nothing went wrong.

detail.description: The offending id, claim or service; empty when not applicable.

stats.description: Running totals across the whole run — the trade expressed in numbers.

accepted.description: Requests served as a known caller.

storeLookups.description: Times a verification had to ask a shared store; always 0 for plain JWTs.

bytesOnTheWire.description: Credential bytes carried across every verified request.

breaches.description: Requests served that should not have been.
